headline: Planning director presented draft zoning changes to meet new state housing laws, including multi-family housing in commercial districts.
summary: The draft updates accessory dwelling unit and tiny house rules to match state law, and a committee will study uses in General Commercial III, near the Robert Frost Farm, after Thanksgiving. Legal counsel at NHMA will be asked whether housing and commercial space can be in separate buildings on one lot. The board also conditionally approved a two-lot subdivision at 20 Lenox Road, with conditions to be met within six months. It approved a sign at 3 East Broadway and accepted a $30,721.68 cash escrow for 35 Maple Street.
decisions: Approved final release of $8,395 letter of credit for Derry Motor Fuel Outlet at 56 Crystal Avenue.
Approved cash escrow of $30,721.68 for 35 Maple Street, non-interest bearing.
Approved sign design for MacDaddy's and a Little More at 3 East Broadway, as presented.
Motion failed to find the 20 Lenox Road subdivision a development of regional impact, with all members voting no.
Approved a waiver from HISS mapping for the 20 Lenox Road subdivision.
Adopted findings that the 20 Lenox Road plan has safe access, meets utility standards, and has enough hydrants.
Conditionally approved the two-lot subdivision at 20 Lenox Road, with conditions to be met within six months.
discussion: State-law zoning changes: The planning director suggested handling changes required by state law first, then inconsistencies within town rules. The draft updates accessory dwelling unit and innovative housing definitions, and sets the tiny house size at 600 square feet or less.

Mixed-use on one lot: Members asked whether a commercial building and a housing building can share one lot, and whether the commercial building must be strictly commercial. They plan to ask legal counsel at NHMA for an opinion.
Density limits: Members said 40 units per acre in the Office Business District may be too dense. They also said 20 units per acre may be too much for the historic area near the Robert Frost Farm.

General Commercial III uses: Members want more study before changing the uses allowed near the Robert Frost Farm, and a committee of the planning board is planned to start after Thanksgiving. A member of the public urged the board not to be overly restrictive in that district.

Adult care in commercial districts: Members agreed to add adult care centers where child care is allowed. They said the child care and adult care rules should match, including whether a license is required.
